text: The Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution takes effect, guaranteeing women the right to vote.
title: Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution
extract: The 19th Amendment prohibits the states and the federal government from denying the right to vote to citizens of the United States on the basis of sex.

text: The National Constituent Assembly of France adopts the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.
title: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
extract: A fundamental document of the French Revolution defining individual and collective rights.

text: The volcano Krakatoa begins its catastrophic final eruptions, one of the most violent in recorded history.
title: 1883 eruption of Krakatoa
extract: The 1883 eruption ejected enormous amounts of rock and ash and was heard thousands of kilometres away.

text: John Fitch is granted a United States patent for the steamboat.
title: John Fitch (inventor)
extract: An American inventor who built the first steam-powered boat in the United States.

text: The Seljuk Turks defeat the Byzantine Empire at the Battle of Manzikert.
title: Battle of Manzikert
extract: A decisive battle that led to the Byzantine loss of much of Anatolia.

text: Cardinal Albino Luciani is elected Pope John Paul I.
title: Pope John Paul I
extract: His 33-day papacy was one of the shortest in history.

text: The Battle of Crecy is fought, a major English victory in the Hundred Years' War.
title: Battle of Crecy
extract: English longbowmen played a decisive role against the French army.

text: The British Motor Corporation launches the Mini, an iconic small car.
title: Mini
extract: A small economy car that became a symbol of 1960s Britain.

text: New Horizons transmits detailed images following its historic flyby of Pluto.
title: New Horizons
extract: A NASA space probe that performed the first flyby of the Pluto system.

text: Robert Walpole, generally regarded as the first Prime Minister of Great Britain, is born.
title: Robert Walpole
extract: A British statesman widely considered the first de facto Prime Minister.

text: Antoine Lavoisier, the father of modern chemistry, is born.
title: Antoine Lavoisier
extract: A French nobleman and chemist central to the 18th-century chemical revolution.

text: Tex Avery, pioneering American animator, dies.
title: Tex Avery
extract: An animator known for creating Daffy Duck and Bugs Bunny's personalities.

text: Women's Equality Day is observed in the United States.
title: Women's Equality Day
extract: Commemorates the adoption of the Nineteenth Amendment.

text: Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first humans to land on the Moon.
title: Apollo 11
extract: The spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon, fulfilling a national goal set by John F. Kennedy.

text: A plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler at the Wolf's Lair fails.
title: 20 July plot
extract: A failed attempt by German military officers to kill Hitler and seize control.

text: The Viking 1 lander becomes the first spacecraft to successfully land on Mars and return images.
title: Viking 1
extract: NASA's Viking 1 was the first US mission to land safely on Mars.

text: Colombia declares independence from Spain.
title: Colombian Declaration of Independence
extract: Marks the beginning of Colombia's independence movement.

text: The Battle of Lissa, the first major naval battle between ironclad warships, is fought.
title: Battle of Lissa (1866)
extract: A naval engagement in the Adriatic between the Italian and Austrian navies.

text: The mathematician and physicist contributions of the era continue as notable figures are born.
title: History of science
extract: The late 19th century saw rapid advances across the sciences.

text: Bruce Lee, martial artist and actor, dies at the age of 32.
title: Bruce Lee
extract: A Hong Kong-American martial artist and actor who founded Jeet Kune Do.
